teams.heading: Jake White emerges as leading candidate for Fiji head coach vacancy
teams.body: Former Springboks boss Jake White has emerged as the leading candidate to become the next Fiji head coach ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. The World Cup-winning coach joins a high-profile field of contenders as Fiji Rugby seeks a permanent successor to Mick Byrne, who departed by mutual agreement in April. With the coaching search intensified, White's pedigree makes him a prominent frontrunner to guide the national team out of their recent slump, following three successive defeats that have left them bottom of the standings.

lead.why: Jake White has emerged as the leading candidate in the ongoing search for the next Flying Fijians head coach.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama trains with French club Provence Rugby during his off-season
teams.body: French club Provence Rugby hosted NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama for training during his summer off-season. The 22-year-old French basketballer, standing at 7ft 4in, spent time working on physical and mental strength with the second-tier side, participating in passing drills, tackle pad work and line-outs. Wembanyama, who also shared a dressing-room embrace with former England international Teimana Harrison, praised the side's camaraderie, calling it a 'great experience' and stating, 'I want to do it again.'

lead.why: It is an intriguing, high-profile cross-sport story about a French basketball superstar training with a French rugby club.

teams.heading: Ireland women secure consecutive victories with a seven-try win over Japan
teams.body: The Ireland women's squad secured consecutive victories over Japan with a comprehensive 43-19 win at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. Scott Bemand's side scored seven tries, recovering from an early deficit to lead 22-7 at half-time. Brittany Hogan and Beibhinn Parsons both crossed the line, with Parsons extending her record to 25 international tries, while debutants Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett scored after coming off the bench. The squad now travels to South Africa for their WXV campaign with significant momentum.

lead.why: Ireland women's comprehensive seven-try victory over Japan completes consecutive wins before their WXV campaign.

teams.heading: Italy sit eleventh in the table following three consecutive tournament defeats
teams.body: Italy sit eleventh in the Nations Championship standings after suffering three straight losses in their opening tournament fixtures. Gonzalo Quesada's men have struggled to find their rhythm, scoring 37 points across those three matches. Defensively, they have conceded 131 points in that same three-game span, a run that culminated in a 10-57 defeat against Australia in their last outing. Historically, the side reached their highest ever world ranking of No. 8 in both 2007 and 2024.

teams.heading: The Welsh Rugby Union slashes ticket prices to £10 for Australia
teams.body: The Welsh Rugby Union has launched a flash sale offering students upper-tier tickets for just £10 in an effort to avoid thousands of empty seats against Australia. More than 44,000 tickets — over half of the stadium's capacity — remain unsold for the final autumn international. Sluggish sales are also affecting Wales' other home fixtures, with around 36,000 tickets still available for the meeting with Japan and 30,000 left for the New Zealand match.

lead.why: The WRU's dramatic ticket price cut to £10 for the Australia match highlights major attendance concerns for the autumn campaign.

teams.heading: Argentina puts forward eight stadiums in joint 2035 World Cup bid
teams.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has submitted its technical proposal to World Rugby, nominating eight domestic stadiums for the joint 2035 Rugby World Cup bid. Argentina is leading the four-nation project alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, with famous venues like Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental and Rio de Janeiro's Maracanã included. Union president Félix Páez Molina hailed the bid as a vital step, as the South American coalition prepares to compete against Japan and Spain before the hosting decision in November 2027.

lead.why: It introduces official comments from union president Félix Páez Molina and highlights the specific stadium submissions for the 2035 World Cup bid.

teams.heading: Tom Hooper returns to Exeter Chiefs after early release from Wallabies squad
teams.body: Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has confirmed Wallabies forward Tom Hooper has returned to England and could feature in Sunday's Premiership match against Newcastle. The 25-year-old was released from the Australia squad ahead of the Bledisloe Cup series because the Tests fall outside World Rugby's regulation nine window. Hooper, who made 23 appearances for Exeter last season, has had a 10-day break and is eager to play, with Baxter noting that if they select him, "it'll be a bench situation."

teams.heading: Steve Lancaster confirms All Blacks will not play Lions in Australia
teams.body: New Zealand Rugby CEO Steve Lancaster has clarified that all matches for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour will take place within Aotearoa. Responding to reports that a Test could be moved to the Melbourne Cricket Ground to maximise revenue, Lancaster stated such a move was not acceptable. While he acknowledged the challenge of balancing limited local stadium capacities with the financial demands of the modern game, he maintained that the team would not prioritise offshore fixtures at the expense of home fans.

lead.why: The CEO's comments provide a significant, new policy update regarding the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour.

teams.heading: World Rugby bans 'hip drop' tackle following Springboks' injury concerns
teams.body: World Rugby has officially outlawed the 'hip drop' and 'knee drop' tackles, effective from 1 November. The decision follows a review by an expert tackle height working group, with the former move specifically targeted after Springboks coach Felix Jones campaigned against the technique. The move comes as a direct response to the impact of such tackles on player welfare, exemplified by the incident that previously sidelined South Africa forward Elrigh Louw for 10 months with severe leg injuries.

lead.why: It reports a significant regulatory change directly influenced by Springbok coaching staff to improve player welfare.
